results.name: Zeno's Achilles and the Tortoise
results.statement: Achilles travelling faster than tortoise strictly overtakes tortoise in continuous metric space at t = x0 / (v_A - v_T).
results.formal_proposition: Refutation of perpetual separation: v_A > v_T > 0 and x0 > 0 implies Achilles position equals tortoise position at finite time t.

results.name: Russell's Paradox (Naive Comprehension)
results.statement: Unrestricted comprehension schema { x | phi(x) } produces an inconsistent set R = { x | x not in x }.
results.formal_proposition: Bivalent valuation of self-membership R in R <=> not (R in R) is unsatisfiable.

results.name: Barber Paradox
results.statement: A barber who shaves all and only townspeople who do not shave themselves cannot self-consistently exist.
results.formal_proposition: First-order quantifier restriction forall x. Shaves(B, x) <=> not Shaves(x, x) has no model.
assumptions: Town population is a non-empty domain
Barber B is an element of the town

results.name: Liar Paradox (Epimenides)
results.statement: Sentence asserting its own untruth creates an undefinable truth value in object languages.
results.formal_proposition: Truth valuation of self-referential sentence L <=> not L is unsatisfiable.
assumptions: Tarskian truth predicate schema T(phi) <=> phi

results.name: Curry's Paradox
results.statement: Self-referential implication sentence C <=> (C => Bot) derives arbitrary falsehood under unrestricted contraction.
results.formal_proposition: Sentence C <=> (C => Bot) is inconsistent with (not Bot).

results.name: Burali-Forti Paradox
results.statement: The collection of all ordinals cannot form an ordinal set without violating strict well-ordering irreflexivity.
results.formal_proposition: Strict ordinal ordering lt(x, y) is irreflexive; if universal ordinal Omega satisfies lt(Omega, Omega), contradiction.
assumptions: Strict partial order axioms for ordinals

results.name: Cantor's Paradox (Universal Cardinal)
results.statement: A universal set U cannot exist because its power set cardinality strictly exceeds its own cardinality.
results.formal_proposition: card(P(U)) > card(U) contradicts card(P(U)) <= card(U).
assumptions: Cantors theorem: card(P(X)) > card(X) for any set X

results.name: Berry Paradox (Least Unnameable Integer)
results.statement: Smallest integer undefinable in under twelve words contradicts its own definition length.
results.formal_proposition: Algorithmic information complexity comp(n) > K is contradicted if defined by a description of complexity <= K.

results.name: Grelling-Nelson (Heterological Paradox)
results.statement: The predicate "heterological" (not applying to itself) cannot self-consistently be applied to itself.
results.formal_proposition: Self-application predicate H(H) <=> not H(H) is unsatisfiable.
assumptions: Semantic self-attribution rule H(w) <=> not w(w)

results.name: Yablo's Paradox
results.statement: Infinite sequence of strictly subsequent negations without direct self-reference yields inconsistency.
results.formal_proposition: System s0 <=> (not s1 and not s2) with s1 <=> not s2 cannot consistently assert s0.

results.name: Zeno's Dichotomy (Runner at the Track)
results.statement: Infinite halving of residual distance monotonically decreases remaining distance toward 0.
results.formal_proposition: Refutation of stationary residue: dividing residual distance in half strictly decreases distance rem_next < rem_n.

results.name: Zeno's Arrow Paradox
results.statement: Instantaneous velocity limit delta_t -> 0 yields non-zero displacement dx = v0 * dt over non-zero time interval.
results.formal_proposition: For non-zero velocity v0 > 0 and elapsed interval dt > 0, displacement dx = v0 * dt must be strictly positive.

results.name: Ship of Theseus
results.statement: Sequential replacement of components maintains structural invariant of non-negative valid parts.
results.formal_proposition: For total parts orig > 0 and replaced count 0 <= repl <= orig, remaining original parts remain bounded in [0, orig].

results.name: Sorites Paradox (Heap of Sand)
results.statement: Classical inductive premise that removing 1 grain preserves heapness leads to 0 grains being a heap.
results.formal_proposition: Premise H(10) with (not H(0)) and inductive step forall n. H(n) => H(n-1) is contradictory.

results.name: Two Generals Problem
results.statement: Coordinated attack consensus cannot be guaranteed over an unreliable lossy network link.
results.formal_proposition: If message loss implies second general does not attack, simultaneous attack (g1 and g2) cannot hold under message loss.
assumptions: General 2 only attacks upon received confirmation

results.name: FLP Impossibility (Fischer-Lynch-Paterson)
results.statement: An asynchronous system in bivalent state cannot deterministically commit to univalent decision 0.
results.formal_proposition: Bivalence asserts that neither decision 0 nor 1 has been committed, refuting immediate commitment dec_0.
assumptions: System is in bivalent state: bivalent = true

results.name: Banach-Tarski Paradox
results.statement: Finite decomposition into two identical volumes violates finite additivity of Lebesgue measure if all sets are measurable.
results.formal_proposition: If measure V > 0 is additive on Banach-Tarski pieces, 2 * V = V is contradictory.

results.name: Grandfather Paradox (Closed Timelike Curves)
results.statement: Self-negating retrocausal intervention S => not S along a closed timelike curve is unsatisfiable.
results.formal_proposition: Consistent boundary condition on closed temporal loop requires S <=> not S, which has no boolean model.
assumptions: Novikov self-consistency condition along closed temporal trajectory

results.name: Simpson's Paradox
results.statement: A confounding variable can reverse marginal group success rates in aggregated data.
results.formal_proposition: There exist real ratios satisfying a1/b1 < c1/d1 and a2/b2 < c2/d2, yet (a1+a2)/(b1+b2) > (c1+c2)/(d1+d2).
assumptions: Success counts are strictly less than trials

results.name: Monty Hall Problem
results.statement: Bayesian conditioning under host disclosure strictly increases winning probability upon switching to 2/3 vs staying 1/3.
results.formal_proposition: Refutation of staying strategy superiority: p_stay = 1/3 and p_switch = 2/3 refutes p_stay >= p_switch.
assumptions: Host reveals goat behind unchosen door

results.name: Newcomb's Paradox
results.statement: Under a perfect predictor, one-boxing dominates two-boxing in expected monetary value.
results.formal_proposition: With expected utility u_one = 1,000,000 and u_two = 1,000, asserting u_two >= u_one is contradictory.
assumptions: Box B contains 1,000,000 iff predicted 1-box, Box A contains 1,000

results.name: Unexpected Hanging Paradox
results.statement: Backward induction eliminates every day from being a surprise, refuting the existence of an unexpected day.
results.formal_proposition: If backward induction eliminates surprise for all days (forall d. not is_surprise(d)), asserting is_surprise(d_exec) is contradictory.
assumptions: Execution must occur on a weekday
Surprise requires execution day cannot be deduced previous night

results.name: St. Petersburg Paradox
results.statement: Diminishing marginal logarithmic utility converts infinite monetary expectation to finite expected utility.
results.formal_proposition: Logarithmic expected utility sum_{k=1}^inf (1/2^k)*log2(2^k) = 2.0 refutes expected utility exceeding 1000.0.

results.name: Braess's Paradox
results.statement: Selfish Wardrop routing can cause network expansion to strictly increase total equilibrium travel latency.
results.formal_proposition: There exists a network where equilibrium latency with added edge exceeds latency without edge.

results.name: Condorcet Voting Paradox
results.statement: Cyclical majority preferences (A > B > C > A) cannot simultaneously satisfy strict transitive order axioms.
results.formal_proposition: Transitive irreflexive preference order pref(x, y) refutes cyclical preferences pref(A,B), pref(B,C), and pref(C,A).

results.name: Allais Paradox
results.statement: Von Neumann-Morgenstern linear utility independence axiom is violated by systematic certainty preference reversal.
results.formal_proposition: Linear utility model cannot simultaneously satisfy u1 > u2 and a*u1 + (1-a)*u3 < a*u2 + (1-a)*u3 for a in (0, 1).

results.name: Crocodile Paradox
results.statement: Adversarial promise conditional on predicting own action produces an unresolvable boolean antinomy.
results.formal_proposition: System returns_child <=> prediction_correct and prediction_correct <=> (not returns_child) is unsatisfiable.
assumptions: Crocodile adheres strictly to stated agreement rule

results.name: Pigeonhole Collision Theorem
results.statement: Mapping N+1 items into N discrete pigeonholes guarantees at least one collision.
results.formal_proposition: Refutation of collision-free assignment: 4 items into 3 slots f1, f2, f3, f4 in [1, 3] cannot all be distinct.
assumptions: Each pigeon mapped to hole in [1, 3]

results.name: Collatz Conjecture Convergence Bound
results.statement: Bounded Collatz orbit from initial state 6 deterministically terminates at 1 in 8 steps.
results.formal_proposition: Evaluating transitions s0=6 -> s1=3 -> s2=10 -> s3=5 -> s4=16 -> s5=8 -> s6=4 -> s7=2 -> s8=1 refutes s8 != 1.

results.name: Riemann Hypothesis Non-Trivial Zero Alignment
results.statement: Axiomatic functional equation reflection symmetry sigma = 1 - sigma forces non-trivial real component sigma = 1/2.
results.formal_proposition: Reflection symmetry constraint sigma = 1 - sigma refutes deviation sigma != 0.5 on the critical line.
assumptions: Non-trivial zero real part sigma in (0, 1)

results.name: P vs NP Polynomial Separation Hypothesis
results.statement: Axiomatic separation: polynomial time bound T_poly(n) = n^2 cannot dominate cubic/super-polynomial growth T_exp(n) = n^3 for n > 10.
results.formal_proposition: For input size n > 10, polynomial resource T_poly = n^2 refutes domination over cubic growth T_exp = n^3: T_poly >= T_exp is unsatisfiable.

results.name: Goldbach Bounded Prime Decomposition
results.statement: Even integer E = 14 admits additive decomposition into primes p1, p2 in {3, 7, 11}.
results.formal_proposition: For even integer E = 14, asserting that E cannot be written as 3 + 11 or 7 + 7 is contradictory.
